## **Margaret Sanger: Reproduktiv frihet eller statlig kontroll?**
### **Kronologisk oversikt over de viktigste hendelsene**

---

### **1902: Giftemål**

citations.cited_text: In 1902, just months before completing the program, **she met and married architect William Sanger**.
citations.title: Sanger, Margaret - Social Welfare History Project

content.text: Ifølge Social Welfare History Project: "In 1902, just months before completing the program, she met and married architect William Sanger"

. Dette markerte starten på Sangers familieliv før hun vendte seg mot aktivisme.

---

### **1912: Møte med Sadie Sachs – vendepunkt**

citations.cited_text:
### Life’s Work
A turning point in Sanger’s life occurred when she met a young mother of three named Sadie Sachs. Sanger was called to nurse Sachs dur...
citations.title: Margaret Sanger

content.text: Ifølge EBSCO: "A turning point in Sanger's life occurred when she met a young mother of three named Sadie Sachs. Sanger was called to nurse Sachs during the sweltering summer of 1912. Sachs had attempted an abortion and was near death when Sanger was called to the apartment."

Dette møtet inspirerte Sangers kamp for prevensjon.

---

### **1914: Lansering av The Woman Rebel**

citations.cited_text: In 1914, Sanger launched her own feminist publication, *The Woman Rebel*, advocating for birth control.
citations.title: Biography: Margaret Sanger

content.text: Ifølge Women's History Institute: "In 1914, Sanger launched her own feminist publication, *The Woman Rebel*, advocating for birth control."

Avisen introduserte også begrepet "birth control".

---

### **1914: Distribusjon av Family Limitation**

citations.cited_text: After twenty refusals, Sanger found a printer for *Family Limitation* . With the help of friends, Sanger began distributing the pamphlet and was arres...
citations.title: Margaret Sanger

content.text: Ifølge EBSCO: "After twenty refusals, Sanger found a printer for *Family Limitation*. With the help of friends, Sanger began distributing the pamphlet and was arrested immediately."

---

### **1915-1916: Flukt til Europa og retur**

citations.cited_text: Sanger remained exiled in Europe until late 1915; William Sanger had been arrested and jailed for distributing one copy of *Family Limitation*, and Ma...
citations.title: Sanger, Margaret - Social Welfare History Project

content.text: Ifølge Social Welfare History Project: "Sanger remained exiled in Europe until late 1915; William Sanger had been arrested and jailed for distributing one copy of *Family Limitation*, and Margaret Sanger returned to face the charges against her. Personal tragedy intervened when the Sangers 5-year-old daughter died suddenly from pneumonia; public sentiments resulted in dismissal of the charges against Margaret Sanger."

---

### **Oktober 16, 1916: Åpning av første prevensjonsklinikk**

citations.cited_text:
# Seventy-Fifth Anniversary of the Brownsville Clinic

On October 16, 1916, Margaret Sanger opened the first American bi...

When the clinic opened on the morning of October 16th, the line of Jewish and Italian immigrant women stretched almost around the block."

The Negro project lasted three years, beginning in 1939 and ending in 1942."
**Kontekst om prosjektet:**

citations.cited_text: Sanger believed that, through the Negro Project, she would help African Americans gain better access to safe contraception and maintain birth control ...

---

### **1942: Pensjonering**

citations.cited_text: Sanger retired in 1942 and moved to Tucson, Arizona, though she remained a passionate advocate for birth control.
citations.title: Biography: Margaret Sanger

content.text: Ifølge Women's History: "Sanger retired in 1942 and moved to Tucson, Arizona, though she remained a passionate advocate for birth control."

citations.title: Biography: Margaret Sanger

content.text: Ifølge Women's History: "In the late 1950s, with funding from International Harvester heiress Katharine McCormick, Sanger recruited researcher Gregory Pincus to develop an oral contraceptive."

### **1960: Godkjenning av prevensjonspillen**

citations.cited_text: In her later life, Sanger spearheaded the effort that resulted in the modern birth control pill by 1960.
citations.title: Biography: Margaret Sanger

content.text: Ifølge Women's History: "In her later life, Sanger spearheaded the effort that resulted in the modern birth control pill by 1960."

citations.cited_text: Sanger lived to see another important reproductive rights milestone in 1965, when the Supreme Court made birth control legal for married couples in it...

content.text: Ifølge Biography.com: "Sanger lived to see another important reproductive rights milestone in 1965, when the Supreme Court made birth control legal for married couples in its decision on *Griswold v.* Connecticut."

citations.cited_text: On 6 September 1966 at the age of 86, Sanger died in Tucson, Arizona, from congestive heart failure.
citations.title: Margaret Higgins Sanger (1879-1966)

content.text: Ifølge ASU Embryo Project: "On 6 September 1966 at the age of 86, Sanger died in Tucson, Arizona, from congestive heart failure."

citations.cited_text: In 2021, Planned Parenthood’s New York chapter removed Sanger’s name from a clinic, acknowledging her “harmful connections to the eugenics movement.”
citations.title: Margaret Sanger, Racist Eugenicist Extraordinaire

content.text: Ifølge ett analysesenter: "In 2021, Planned Parenthood's New York chapter removed Sanger's name from a clinic, acknowledging her 'harmful connections to the eugenics movement.'"

## **1. HENNES GRUNNLEGGENDE ARBEID FOR REPRODUKTIV FRIHET**
